name: haiku-v2-3
how: Each session: a fresh Claude Code subagent that could read only the rendered prompts (one file per case), answered them in order and wrote its answers to a file. No API key; nothing else in its context.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: The only assertion checks the URL before Cancel is clicked and nothing checks where Cancel leads, so a wrong destination passes.

answers.test: cancel returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: After clicking Cancel on the overview the URL is asserted to match inventory.html, so Cancel going to the cart or elsewhere would fail.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: Going directly to /inventory.html after logout and checking the error text would fail if the message were wrong or missing.

answers.test: cart badge is cleared after finishing @regression
answers.reason: The badge count is asserted to be zero after finishing, so a badge still showing would fail.

answers.test: removing a product decrements the badge @regression
answers.reason: Removing one of two items and asserting the badge reads 1 would fail if the decrement were wrong or missing.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: After reset the test asserts the URL is inventory.html and the Products title, so a logout or wrong page would fail.

answers.test: clicking a product name opens its details page @smoke
answers.reason: Clicking the product link and asserting the URL matches inventory-item.html?id=4 would fail if the name link did not open the details page.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: The details page name and price are asserted equal to the list values, so a wrong name or price would fail.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: It only asserts the error is visible, so a missing error fails but an error with the wrong message passes.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The total check only asserts the label contains 'Total: $', so a wrong total amount passes.

answers.test: item stays in the cart after opening another product @smoke
answers.reason: After opening another product's details page and then the cart, the backpack is asserted to be listed, so an emptied cart would fail.

answers.test: valid credentials redirect to the products page @smoke
answers.reason: A valid login is asserted to land on inventory.html, so a failed or wrong redirect would fail.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: After logout the login button must be visible, which only holds on the login page, so a logout that does not return there would fail.

answers.test: cart badge is cleared after finishing @regression
answers.reason: The only test for the badge after finishing is test.skip, so it never runs and no other test checks the badge.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The exact text 'Error: Last Name is required' is asserted after filling only the first name, so a wrong or missing message would fail.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: Only the High to Low sort is tried for the six-product count, so a broken count under the other sorts would pass.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: The error text containing 'Username is required' is asserted after an empty login, so a missing or different message would fail.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The total label is asserted to read exactly 'Total: $32.39', so a wrong amount would fail.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: The six-product assertion was replaced by a count that is always at least 0, so it can never fail.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: The first product name and its price are asserted for the low-to-high sort, so a wrong first product or price would fail.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The exact text 'Error: First Name is required' is asserted after clicking Continue with empty fields.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: The first product name is checked for the low-to-high sort but the $7.99 price is not asserted in this test, so a wrong price would pass.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: The tax label is asserted to read exactly 'Tax: $2.40'.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: The login error is asserted to contain 'Username is required' after submitting an empty form.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: After reset the cart page is asserted to have zero inventory items, so leftover items would fail.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: The URL and the 'Checkout: Complete!' text are asserted after Finish, so a wrong page would fail.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: The single-add test only checks visibility, but the two-product test asserts an exact badge count of 2, which would catch a wrong increment.

answers.test: overview lists the backpack @smoke
answers.reason: The overview item names are asserted to be exactly the backpack, so a wrong or missing item would fail.

answers.test: adding a product sets the cart badge to 1 @smoke
answers.reason: The badge is asserted to read exactly '1' after adding one product.

answers.test: locked-out user sees a locked-out message @regression
answers.reason: The error is asserted to contain the exact locked-out message.

answers.test: logout returns to the login page @smoke
answers.reason: After logout the URL is asserted to equal the base login URL, so a different landing page would fail.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: After removing the only item the badge is asserted to have a count of zero, so a visible badge would fail.

answers.test: all fields filled continues to the overview @regression
answers.reason: Filling all fields and asserting the title reads 'Checkout: Overview' would fail if Continue did not advance.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: After reloading the products page the badge is asserted to read 1, so losing the count would fail.

answers.test: item total is $29.99 @regression
answers.reason: The item total label is asserted to read exactly 'Item total: $29.99'.

answers.test: missing postal code shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The postal code error is asserted to read exactly 'Error: Postal Code is required'.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: Clicking Cancel and asserting the URL matches cart.html checks the named cart page.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: Adding two products and asserting the badge reads exactly 2 would fail for a wrong count.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: The URL and the Checkout Complete text are asserted after Finish, so a wrong page would fail.

answers.test: cart page lists the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The cart item names are asserted to equal the two added products exactly.

answers.test: back home returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: After clicking Back Home the URL is asserted to match inventory.html, which names the products page.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The login button is asserted visible after logout, which only holds if the user is back on the login page.

answers.test: name Z to A shows the red T-shirt first @regression
answers.reason: The first product under Z to A is asserted to be the red T-shirt by exact name.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: The details page is never asserted: the test only checks the list values are truthy and the click has no following assertion.

answers.test: default sort is name A to Z with Sauce Labs Backpack first @smoke
answers.reason: The sort dropdown value and the first product name are asserted for the default sort.

answers.test: checkout opens the Your Information step @smoke
answers.reason: The title is asserted to read exactly 'Checkout: Your Information' after clicking Checkout.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: The incorrect-password test clicks login and has no assertion, so no outcome is checked.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: The test removing the last item asserts the page title is Products instead of the badge, so the badge is never checked.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: The error text containing 'Username and password do not match' is asserted after a wrong password.

answers.test: back to products returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: After Back to products the URL is asserted to match inventory.html, which names the products page.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: It checks the menu button is visible but not the products page URL or title, so a reset that lands on another logged-in page would pass.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The two-item cart test asserts only the count of 2, not the item names, so a wrong second item would pass.

answers.test: products page displays at least one product after login @regression
answers.reason: The first product in the list is asserted visible after login, so an empty products page would fail.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: The badge is asserted to read exactly '1' after adding from the details page.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: The first product name and its price are asserted for the high-to-low sort.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It asserts only that the error contains the word required, so a wrong message such as the first-name error would pass.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The cart item names are asserted to equal the two added products exactly.

answers.test: reset removes the cart badge @smoke
answers.reason: The cart badge is asserted to have a count of zero after reset.

answers.test: thank-you heading is shown @regression
answers.reason: The complete header text is asserted to read exactly 'Thank you for your order!'.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: The check uses the unanchored regex /2.4/, so a near-miss amount such as 2.41 or 2.45 would pass while a missing label would fail.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The login-button assertion sits in a try/catch that only logs, so it can never fail.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: The badge assertion is not awaited, so the test finishes without waiting on it and a wrong count would not reliably fail.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: It counts a cart-item data-test selector that does not exist on saucedemo, so it always reads zero and passes whether or not items remain.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: The badge check runs only if the badge is already visible, so a missing badge would pass while a wrong count would fail.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The assertion only checks the error is not the last-name message, which passes for almost any wrong outcome.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: The test navigates back to the products page and asserts the badge reads 1, so losing the cart count on a fresh load would fail.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: The high-to-low criterion is tested by selecting Low to High and checking the last item, and the six-product test checks only the count, so a broken high-to-low sort would pass.
